Filipino consumers face price hikes as Goldman Sachs warns of renewed inflation. Filipino consumers face a renewed risk of higher retail prices as manufacturers move to pass escalating production costs onto buyers, according to a Goldman Sachs Group Inc. report obtained by the Manila Bulletin. In the commentary, Goldman Sachs economists Chris Poh and Danny Suwanapruti noted that companies are preparing to offset persistent supply chain disruptions and higher input expenses by raising consumer prices. The re-escalation of conflict in the Middle East has pushed production costs higher, signaling intensifying inflationary pressures across the manufacturing sector. Despite these cost pressures, domestic industrial activity showed resilience in July. S&P Global’s Philippines Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 51.8 in July from 50.9 in June, its third consecutive monthly rise and bringing the headline index broadly in line with its long-run average. The acceleration to a five-month high was driven by stronger demand, which lifted output and new orders. A PMI reading above 50 indicates expansion in the sector. However, manufacturing indicators point to a potential rebound in price pressures, even as broader inflation figures show near-term relief. Headline inflation slowed to 6.2 percent in July—its lowest level in three months since peaking at 7.2 percent in April. Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy items, also continued to moderate. Goldman Sachs pointed out that despite the July dip, inflation remained above the midpoint of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ (BSP) forecast range of 5.6 percent to 6.6 percent, and far above the government’s 4.0 percent target ceiling. The central bank currently projects inflation to average 6.4 percent this year and 4.5 percent in 2027—both well above official targets. Upward price risks driven by imported oil and elevated production costs are expected to keep monetary authorities on high alert. Since Middle East hostilities flared up in late February, the BSP has raised its benchmark borrowing rate twice, bringing key interest rates to 4.75 percent. The Monetary Board will hold its fourth policy meeting of the year on Aug. 27, followed by scheduled sessions on Oct. 22 and Dec. 17.

Taiwan’s military drills suggest deeper alignment with the US. TAIPEI, Taiwan (AP) — Through this year’s military drills, Taiwan has chosen to emphasize its army's and society’s flexibility and resilience as opposed to primarily putting advanced weapons on display. Experts say the exercises’ structure indicates closer ties with the U.S. military in the face of China’s ongoing military threat . The annual Huang Kuang drills kicked off on Wednesday and are set to extend through Aug. 14 in various locations around the island. The live-fire exercises will test the Taiwanese army’s ability to sustain 24-hour defense operations as well as counter China’s “gray-zone tactics,” which stop just short of open warfare. China claims the self-ruled democracy as its own territory, and has not renounced the use of force to bring it under its control. Taiwan dismisses China’s claims and insists it is a sovereign state. The United States, while not recognizing Taiwan as a country, sees all threats to the island as a matter of great concern. Washington is bound by its own laws to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself. The drills show closer ties with the US military While there has long been speculation that the U.S. military has been quietly training Taiwanese troops, the collaboration between the two sides has been more visible in recent weeks. A key component of the Han Kuang drills, for example, is the practice of a U.S.-inspired military communications method called backbriefing, where subordinates explain to commanders how they plan to carry out assigned missions. The communication drills are intended to encourage first-line fighters to be more self-reliant and effective in battle, experts say. “The most important new development in this year’s Han Kuang is the incorporation of American-style military training methods, which are aimed at enhancing the coordination and combat readiness of the Taiwanese military,” said William Yang, a senior Northeast Asia analyst for the International Crisis Group. The drills thus “stay away from the mostly performative tasks of firepower display” of past years and instead focus on building real combat capabilities, Yang added. Emphasis on reservists and urban resilience Another focus of this year’s drills is that they will mobilize one of the largest numbers yet of reservists, of around 20,000 personnel, according to local media. Taiwan’s Defense Ministry did not say how many reservists will be involved in the drills. The emphasis on reserves illustrates Taiwan’s efforts to address the military power asymmetry between itself and China, Yang said. China maintains the world’s largest army, of more than 2 million active-duty personnel, almost nine times the size of Taiwan’s active-duty armed forces. Another focus of the military drills, reflecting Taiwan’s longstanding emphasis on civil defense , are urban resilience drills. These will take place on different days in the major cities of Kaohsiung, Taichung and the capital, Taipei. During the drills, mobile internet speed will be reduced for about 30 minutes to simulate telecommunications interference in case of an attack. The emphasis on combat readiness and civilian preparedness reflect Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te’s priorities amid political constraints, said Lev Nachman, a political-science professor at National Taiwan University. Lai has sought to pass a $40 billion special defense budget for U.S. arms purchases and local defense manufacturing. A much smaller version of the budget, of $24.8 billion, was eventually approved by the opposition-controlled parliament. “Given that Lai has been constrained on his ability to pass a budget that could even supply the kinds of weapons he would want to test, he has had to look to what he is able to do given the domestic political gridlock,” Nachman said. US arms sales to Taiwan remain in question Despite closer informal ties between the U.S. and Taiwan militaries, questions remain around a massive $14 billion arms sales package to Taiwan that U.S. President Donald Trump has yet to approve. After traveling to China in May , Trump described arms sales to Taiwan as a “very good negotiating chip” with Beijing, raising anxieties on the island about continued U.S. support. Trump also said after his summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping that he does not want to “travel 9,500 miles (15,300 kilometers) to fight a war” over Taiwan. In that context, seeing the U.S. influence on Taiwan’s military drills offers a “silver lining” in terms of Washington's commitment to Taiwan, Nachman said. “Even though Trump and those close to him have flip-flopped on supporting Taiwan, the connection between the two militaries remains strong, enough to at least ensure that Taiwan is still able to learn at a high level from the U.S.,” he said. Soldiers conduct shooting training during the annual Han Kuang military exercises in Taipei, Taiwan, Wednesday, Aug. 5, 2026. (AP Photo/Chiang Ying-ying)

What happens to nature long after the shaking stops?. Before the tragedy reaches the headlines, an earthquake has already begun reshaping the environment. When most people think of earthquakes, they picture collapsed buildings, shattered roads, and frightened communities. News reports often focus on the number of casualties, damaged infrastructure, and rescue operations. The recent earthquake in Mindanao was no different, as the death toll rose and more than a million residents were affected. Yet beyond the human tragedy lies another victim—the environment. One of the most immediate consequences of earthquakes is the alteration of landscapes. Powerful ground movement can create ground fissures, trigger landslides, and permanently change the shape of landforms. These changes can affect ecosystems for years after the shaking ends. A clear example occurred during the magnitude 7.2 Bohol earthquake in 2013. According to the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS), satellite imagery revealed that parts of Bohol experienced significant ground uplift, permanently changing the island's terrain. The earthquake also triggered numerous landslides in mountainous areas, stripping vegetation from slopes and altering natural drainage systems. What appeared to be a single moment of destruction left changes to the landscape that persisted long after damaged structures had been repaired. Earthquakes can also transform coastal environments. During the magnitude 7.8 earthquake that struck Mindanao in June 2026, PHIVOLCS reported coastal uplift in parts of Sarangani and Davao Occidental. Previously submerged areas emerged above sea level, exposing portions of shorelines and coral reefs. While such changes may seem minor, they can disrupt delicate marine ecosystems. Coral reefs, seagrass beds, and coastal habitats depend on stable conditions. Sudden shifts in land elevation can affect marine species that rely on these ecosystems for food, breeding, and shelter. Another issue linked to earthquakes is liquefaction. This phenomenon occurs when water-saturated soil loses its strength during intense shaking and temporarily behaves like a liquid. During the Mindanao earthquake, PHIVOLCS documented liquefaction in several affected communities, resulting in ground fissures, land subsidence, and sediment eruptions. Liquefaction can have long-term consequences for both the environment and agriculture. Productive farmland may become unstable, drainage patterns can change, and vegetation may struggle to recover in affected areas. Water resources are also vulnerable. Earthquakes can alter river channels, damage watersheds, and affect underground water systems. Landslides triggered by earthquakes may block rivers, creating temporary natural dams that increase the risk of flooding. In some cases, disturbed soil and debris can reduce water quality and harm aquatic ecosystems. Wildlife is often an overlooked casualty of seismic events. Habitat destruction caused by landslides, coastal changes, and vegetation loss can force animals to relocate or compete for limited resources. Species already facing pressures from deforestation and climate change may find it even harder to adapt to sudden disruptions. Despite these challenges, nature possesses an extraordinary ability to recover. Forests can regenerate, rivers can carve new paths, and ecosystems can gradually rebuild themselves. However, recovery often takes years or even decades, depending on the severity of the damage. Environmental experts emphasize the importance of integrating ecosystem protection into disaster response and recovery plans. Reforestation projects, watershed management, and careful land-use planning can help reduce the risks associated with earthquakes. Monitoring vulnerable ecosystems after major seismic events is also crucial to understanding and addressing long-term impacts. The recent earthquake in Mindanao serves as a reminder that disasters affect more than just people and infrastructure. Beneath the statistics and headlines is an environment that also bears the scars of these natural events. Recognizing the environmental effects of earthquakes is essential for protecting ecosystems and building more resilient communities. As rebuilding begins, the story of an earthquake should not end with damaged buildings. The environment bears its own scars, often long after the shaking stops. For the Philippines, a nation perched on the Pacific Ring of Fire, understanding these impacts is essential to building communities that are not only prepared for the next disaster but resilient enough to recover from it.

Athlete of the soul: A review of 'Just Javier'. One of the films opening in cinemas in the week of Aug. 12 is the Bosco Films documentary "Solo Javier" (to be released as "Just Javier"). It's a biopic of the life of the Spaniard Javier Sartorius, and it chronicles his spiritual transformation and life journey. Coincidentally, the film arrives here on the 20th anniversary of his passing away in 2006. Javier was born into Spanish aristocracy, was a noted tennis player, then a paddle tennis champion in the USA, a surfer, and a coach. But beyond these activities as a regular young man, there was his slow realization that there had to be more to his life than the endless partying, the flirting and dalliances with young women, and this carefree attitude to life. What the documentary faithfully records is his life's transformation and how, at one juncture, Javier dedicated his life to one of meaning, compassion, and a commitment to his faith. Directed by Josep Maria Anglès, and starring Tomas Farell as Javier, the film was crowdfunded, with the full support of the Sartorius family. The brother and cousin of Javier are among the resource persons interviewed in the documentary, and they lend authenticity to the enterprise. Shot in Spain, Peru, and the United States, I appreciated the production values brought to this film, the vistas and drone shots, and how expansive the location shoots are. During the advanced screening that I watched, someone even commented how some of the shots were like travel promos, and that she now wanted to visit Peru. These all belie the fact that the film had been crowdsourced for financing. There is a shine and polish to this documentary. Dubbed in English for its screening here, that may be the only thing one needs to adjust to. I'm fine with subtitles, but I know that here in the Philippines, that's not very popular, and dubbing is more the way to go if one wants the film to be avidly watched. The documentary speaks for itself and is recommended for those who are partial to films of spiritual transformation, of conversion, and about dedicating one's life to a cause. It's a very accessible film, kept relatively linear, and can be admired for being so earnest and sincere. I understand there is a move at the Vatican for the beatification of Javier Sartorius. If you wanted a film depicting what a modern-day saint could be like, this is the film for you. "Just Javier" will be showing exclusively in Ayala Cinemas.

Europe heat wave puts all major Italian cities on red alert. ROME (AP) — Italy placed all its major cities under the highest heat alert Thursday as a blistering heat wave gripped Europe, setting a national temperature record in Austria, fueling wildfires in France and disrupting energy and transport systems across the continent. The extreme weather has pushed temperatures above 40 Celsius (104 Fahrenheit) in several countries, prompting health warnings for millions of people. Scientists and officials warn that such events are becoming more frequent and intense as the climate warms . The current heat wave has exposed vulnerabilities in public health systems, power generation, transportation networks and tourism infrastructure, forcing governments and businesses to adapt to more frequent periods of extreme weather. Italy's red alert in all major cities is a first Italy’s Health Ministry placed all 27 cities monitored under its national heat surveillance system on red alert Thursday — the first time this year that the entire network has been under the highest warning level simultaneously. The alerts stretch from Trieste in the northeast to Palermo in Sicily and signal a health risk for the entire population, not only vulnerable groups such as older adults and people with chronic illnesses. Authorities urged residents and tourists to avoid direct sunlight during the hottest hours of the day, remain indoors where possible and drink plenty of water. The heat has also forced adjustments at major tourist attractions. The ministries of tourism and culture extended evening opening hours at landmarks including Rome’s Colosseum and Pantheon. Mist fans and an 'urban beach' set up to cool residents Cooling mist fans have been installed at the Colosseum’s entrances and additional medical stations have been made available. Rome has also introduced another unusual response to the heat emergency: a free municipal “urban beach” along the Tiber River in the Marconi neighborhood, where residents can cool off in swimming pools, water fountains and shaded areas. The site, known as Tiberis, has become a refuge for families and children seeking relief from record temperatures. Residents praised the initiative, saying it allowed them to better cope with the heat and offered a rare opportunity to escape the city’s scorching asphalt and concrete. “It is excellent, it is a great initiative. They did the right thing, specially with such hot days it is important to cool down with water, specially for children," Rome resident Claudio Rocchi said. Austria and Slovakia break national temperature records Later on Thursday, Slovakia recorded another all-time high temperature. The new record set at Dolne Plachtince in the south was 42.2 C (108 F), the Slovak Meteorological Institute said. In Slovakia, the low levels of water in the Danube forced the country’s biggest hydroelectric power plant in Gabčíkovo to shut down seven of its eight turbines, the TASR news agency said. So far this year, the power plant produced 15% less electricity than a year ago due to a lack of water in the river. The authorities recorded the lowest flow of water in the Danube for July on record, the Academy of Sciences said. An all-time high temperature of 41.2 C (106.2 F) was also recorded in Austria on Wednesday in the village of Bad Deutsch-Altenburg near the Slovak border, according to GeoSphere Austria. Austria is also facing severe drought. Rainfall from Jan. 1 through June 30 was 27% below the long-term average nationwide, while some eastern regions received only half their normal precipitation. Climatologist Alexander Orlik said some parts of the country had not experienced such dry conditions since 1885. Hungary cuts power use as drought hits nuclear plant In Hungary, prolonged drought and record-low water levels on the Danube River have severely affected the country’s only nuclear power plant, which relies on river water to cool its reactors. Plant operators have reduced output to about 10% of normal production, prompting the government to introduce emergency conservation measures as a record-breaking heat wave grips the country. Authorities have asked major industrial users and households to cut electricity consumption, particularly during peak demand hours between 5 p.m. and 10 p.m. Freight trains have been barred from operating during those hours, while decorative lighting on landmarks in Budapest has been switched off. Several major companies, including energy company Mol, pharmaceutical maker Gedeon Richter and automakers Suzuki, Mercedes-Benz, Audi and BMW have announced plans to curb electricity use. The government also canceled parliamentary sessions this week in an effort to conserve power. The heat wave has shattered temperature records across the country. On Wednesday night, Budapest recorded its warmest overnight temperature on record, with temperatures falling only to 28 C (82 F), underscoring the persistence of the extreme heat. Germany worries about shrinking rivers Germany faced growing concerns over the impact of drought on transportation and industry as water levels on the Rhine and other rivers continued to fall. Transport Minister Steffen Bilger met affected organizations Thursday and warned that low water levels posed major challenges for inland waterway shipping, industry and the broader logistics chain. Environmental group BUND urged authorities to focus not only on the economic impacts but also on making rivers more resilient to climate change by retaining more water in landscapes and reducing withdrawals during periods of drought. France remains on high wildfire alert In southeastern France, firefighters maintained a large presence in the Var region after authorities said a major wildfire there was no longer spreading but remained capable of reigniting. The blaze, which began July 20, has burned more than 60 square kilometers (23 square miles), making it the largest recorded in the region in recent decades. Authorities warned that strong winds and extremely dry conditions left southeastern France at very high risk for additional wildfires. Temperatures cooled in England, but the impact from the driest July on record was on display as a grass fire temporarily shut down the southern runway at Heathrow Airport in London on Thursday. Balkans battle fires and drought The heat wave reached its peak across the Balkans on Thursday as temperatures neared 40 C (104 F) and authorities battled drought and wildfires. In Serbia, firefighters struggled to contain several blazes after days of dry weather. One major fire burned through pine forests west of Belgrade, while another spread near the central town of Kraljevo, where difficult terrain complicated firefighting efforts. In neighboring Croatia, tourists in Dubrovnik sought refuge in shade and avoided beaches during the hottest hours of the day as temperatures soared along the Adriatic coast.

The Property Geek: The best time to buy real estate is when everyone else hesitates. Every real estate cycle has one thing in common: people always find a reason to wait. Today, it's inflation. Tomorrow, it could be elections. Next year, it might be interest rates, global conflicts, or economic uncertainty. The headlines change, but the hesitation remains the same. Ironically, this is often when the smartest real estate investors make their move. We're currently in what many would consider a buyer's market. Developers are offering longer and more flexible down payment terms, attractive discounts, and payment schemes that were rarely available during periods of high demand. For buyers with a long-term perspective, these conditions create opportunities that may not exist once the market gains momentum again. History has shown that real estate moves in cycles. Markets slow down, stabilize, recover, and eventually grow. While no one can predict exactly when the next upswing will happen, one thing has remained remarkably consistent: quality real estate appreciates over time. The biggest mistake many aspiring investors make is believing they should only buy when the economy feels perfect. In reality, by the time everyone becomes confident again, prices have often already increased, incentives have disappeared, and competition has returned. Legendary investor Warren Buffett once said, "Be fearful when others are greedy, and greedy when others are fearful." While his advice was directed toward the stock market, the same principle applies to real estate. Opportunity often hides behind uncertainty. This doesn't mean buying recklessly. It means investing wisely. Choose projects from reputable developers, prioritize locations with strong long-term growth drivers, and ensure that your purchase aligns with your financial capacity. Real estate should never be an emotional decision; it should be a strategic one. One advantage today's buyers enjoy is time. Extended payment terms allow many families and investors to secure tomorrow's property values while spreading out today's financial commitment. That's a luxury that often disappears when demand returns. Real estate has survived financial crises, political transitions, pandemics, and global conflicts. Yet cities continue to expand, infrastructure continues to improve, and land remains one of the few assets that cannot be created. Markets will eventually recover, as they always do. The question is not whether opportunities will disappear. The question is whether you'll still be watching from the sidelines when they do. Sometimes, the best investment decisions are made not when the market feels safest, but when you have the courage to see what others don't.

Carney says US trade talks are ‘nasty’ after Trump criticizes Canada’s leadership. TORONTO (AP) — Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Thursday that trade negotiations with the United States had turned “nasty” after President Donald Trump derided America’s neighbor and its leadership while threatening to expand tariffs. Carney said Canada remained engaged in the negotiations despite Trump’s comments, describing the talks as a fight to protect Canadian workers and businesses. “This is a tough negotiation,” Carney said in French. “You can say ‘nasty.’ But this is a question of Canadian jobs. It’s a question of the future of Canadian businesses.” Trump criticized Canada during a speech Wednesday in Las Vegas. “Canada’s nasty. They are. They’re nasty,” Trump said. “I love the people, but they’re nasty. Nasty leadership.” Carney said “we are in the middle of a tariff war with the Americans” but laughed when asked about Trump’s description. He said Canadian negotiators were in Washington this week and that he expected further conversations with Trump after speaking with him last week. The United States already has tariffs on Canadian steel, aluminum and automobiles. Trump has threatened to impose 50% tariffs on more Canadian goods beginning Aug. 19. Tariffs are taxes on imports, which companies can then pass along to consumers in the form of higher prices. The president maintains that the costs created by tariffs will cause manufacturing to relocate to the U.S., though there is little evidence of that in the economic data. Trump’s tariff threats and repeated suggestions that Canada should become the 51st U.S. state have angered many Canadians, prompting many Canadians to cancel trips to the United States. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer has argued that Canada and China are the only two countries to retaliate against Trump’s tariffs, citing restrictions on U.S. alcohol sales in some Canadian provinces among his concerns. Canadian officials say their countermeasures were a response to existing U.S. tariffs. The latest comments followed months of escalating tensions. At the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, in January, Carney criticized major powers for using economic coercion against smaller countries, prompting Trump to respond: “Canada lives because of the United States. Remember that, Mark, the next time you make your statements.” Canada is one of the United States’ largest trading partners, and the move threatens to push prices higher at a time when Americans are already frustrated with the high cost of living ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections. Carney said existing U.S. tariffs on aluminum have contributed to a 58% increase in aluminum prices in the United States. “That’s not a good situation for American companies,” Carney said.

Police probe abandoned caskets in Metro Manila. Police are investigating the abandoned caskets found in five areas across Metro Manila early Friday, Aug. 7, as authorities work to identify those responsible for leaving the items in public places. The National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) said the caskets were discovered in Sta. Cruz, Manila; Barangay 54 in Caloocan City; Barangay South Triangle and Barangay Sta. Teresita in Quezon City; and along Gil Puyat Avenue in Makati City. Initial investigation showed that unidentified masked individuals left the caskets between 2 a.m. and 4 a.m. after arriving aboard gray and white vans, according to the NCRPO. “The Chief PNP has ordered a comprehensive probe to determine the facts and circumstances surrounding the incidents. NCRPO investigators are now on the ground conducting thorough backtracking and forward tracking of CCTV footages,” the NCRPO said. Authorities said the abandoned caskets carried anti-CPP-NPA and anti-China messages. In Quezon City, the Quezon City Police District (QCPD) confirmed that two caskets with attached banners were found at Boy Scout Circle in Barangay South Triangle and Welcome Rotunda in Barangay Sta. Teresita. Responding police officers secured the areas and inspected the caskets, which were found to contain only crumpled papers. The banners attached to the caskets bore the messages “CHINESE COMMUNIST PARTY (CCP) GREEDY! SALOT” and “GREEDY SALOT,” the QCPD said. The QCPD has formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to determine the motive, identify those responsible, and trace the vehicle used in the incidents. The caskets have been taken into police custody for further examination, while authorities are coordinating with relevant establishments to determine the source of the recovered items. Authorities have yet to identify those behind the incidents. They assured the public that the investigation remains ongoing and that appropriate charges will be filed against those responsible.

5.4-magnitude quake jolts Occidental Mindoro. A strong earthquake shook Occidental Mindoro and nearby provinces on Friday morning, Aug. 7, according to the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs). The quake occurred at 10:38 a.m. and was traced 13 kilometers southwest of Mamburao, Occidental Mindoro. It had a shallow depth of 14 kilometers and was tectonic in origin. Phivolcs later revised the earthquake's magnitude to 5.4 from the initial magnitude 5.8 released shortly after the event. The earthquake was felt at Intensity V (strong) in Mamburao in Occidental Mindoro, and in Calapan City, Naujan, Puerto Galera, San Teodoro, and Victoria in Oriental Mindoro. Intensity IV shaking (moderately strong) was experienced in Taal in Batangas, and Abra de Ilog and Sablayan in Oriental Mindoro. Intensity III (weak) was reported in Quezon City in Metro Manila, Batangas City in Batangas, General Trias City in Cavite, and San Pedro City in Laguna. Intensity II (slightly felt) was also reported in Parañaque City in Metro Manila, Santa Cruz in Laguna, and Guinayangan in Quezon. Phivolcs said no damage had been reported but warned that aftershocks may occur.

Waltz turns quiet acts of kindness into new single 'Alitaptap'. Some people drift into our lives sans fanfare, yet end up leaving the biggest mark. They may not stay forever, but their presence comes at the right time, offering comfort, encouragement or simply the reassurance that someone is there when it matters most. It is this quiet kind of connection that inspired OPM singer-songwriter Waltz's latest single, "Alitaptap." "May mga tao na parang ganito. Hindi sila laging nandiyan. Pero kapag nandiyan sila, sobrang liwanag," he said, explaining the idea behind the song. Waltz said he hopes listeners will relate it to their own experiences with people who helped them through difficult times. Its chorus, built around the line "Akin ka na," is meant to express a quiet hope instead of a sweeping declaration of love. The release also marks the launch of "#AkingAlitaptap," a campaign encouraging listeners to share stories about the people who became a source of strength during some of their darkest moments. "Gusto ko hindi lang basta pakinggan ang kanta. Gusto kong ma-feel ng tao na kanya rin siya — kasi baka siya rin, may sariling alitaptap na hindi pa niya nasasabi kung gaano kahalaga," Waltz said. Selected stories will be featured in a series of online videos in which Waltz reads fan submissions. "Alitaptap" follows Waltz's previous single, "Marahuyo." Released under Ant Savvy Artist Management (AS Creatives & Entertainment Inc.) and distributed by Symphonic, "Alitaptap" is now available on major streaming platforms.

Temus backs Filipina-founded Thinking Machines to scale enterprise AI across Southeast Asia. Temus, a Singapore-based AI and digital transformation company established by Temasek, today announced a strategic investment in Thinking Machines Data Science, a Filipina-founded AI and data company headquartered in the Philippines and OpenAI's first official Services Partner in Asia Pacific. The investment marks a recognition of Philippine-built AI talent and capability. Founded in Manila, Thinking Machines has built a decade-long track record in data platforms, AI implementation, and enterprise AI delivery across Southeast Asia. By joining forces with Temus, the company will bring that expertise to a wider regional client base, supported by Temus' enterprise transformation capabilities, scale, and delivery infrastructure. Together, the two companies aim to help enterprises move beyond pilots and embed AI into real workflows that create measurable business value. Across Southeast Asia, companies are moving from AI experimentation to implementation. Many still face the same practical barriers: fragmented data, legacy systems, complex workflows, and talent gaps to design AI-native workflows. The partnership brings together the capabilities required to address those challenges, from data engineering and governance to workflow integration, AI deployment, executive enablement, and workforce capability building. For clients, this means broader access to end-to-end AI and digital transformation support. Thinking Machines brings specialist AI and data execution, regional delivery experience, and OpenAI-enabled services. Temus brings enterprise reach, transformation infrastructure, and experience working with public and private sector organisations across healthcare, financial services, education, and government. "We built Thinking Machines on the belief that the Philippines can build up and scale world-class AI capability," said Stephanie Sy, Founder and CEO, Thinking Machines Data Science; Managing Director, Applied AI & Data, Temus. Joining the Temus group allows us to pursue that ambition at a much greater scale while staying true to our team, our clients, and our mission," she added. Thinking Machines was founded in Manila in 2015 by Stephanie Sy. Over the past decade, the company has trained more than 10,000 professionals in AI and deployed hundreds of AI systems into production with organisations across financial services, retail, conglomerates, and the civic sector. It operates offices in Manila, Singapore, and Bangkok. Its recognition as OpenAI's first APAC Services Partner and now awarded OpenAI advanced partner status, reflects a track record of deploying AI systems across diverse operating environments in the region. Against this backdrop, the Temus investment signals growing confidence in Philippine-built AI talent and innovation. With Thinking Machines' track record across diverse operating environments in the region, the investment opens opportunities for local enterprises to access advanced AI, data foundations, workflow transformation, and adoption support. Accelerating production-grade AI deployment across Southeast Asia Temus, 500-strong and anchored in Singapore, provides full-stack AI transformation spanning cloud and application engineering, consulting, and design. Its work supports Singapore’s Smart Nation and National AI Strategy priorities, with a growing regional presence across Southeast Asia. The partnership combines Temus’ transformation delivery infrastructure with Thinking Machines’ experience in building data platforms and deploying enterprise AI systems. Together, the two firms are positioned to help organisations build the foundations, talent, and repeatable delivery systems needed to make AI work at scale. “Many enterprises are navigating the challenge of running AI systems that hold up under real operating conditions - constrained data, regulatory requirements, complex workflows. That requires a different level of engineering, governance, and integration. Thinking Machines brings deep capability in that layer of the problem. This investment connects two parts of the system that need to work as one: how AI is built, and how it is made to operate at scale.” said Sng Ren Yeong, Chief Executive Officer, Temus. "This investment is a recognition of shared mission - two teams that were each built by people who came home to build. Thinking Machines gains the reach and resources of the Temus group. Temus gains a team that has been doing serious AI delivery work for over a decade. Together, we are better placed than ever to help organisations move from AI pilots into production, for Singapore and beyond." he added.

UP loses to Chinese team in AUBL. University of the Philippines pulled off a solid quarterfinal performance but lost balance in late game to stumble against Tsinghua University, 81-85, and end its podium bid in the 2026 Asian University Basketball League (AUBL) at the Binjiang Gymnasium in Hangzhou, China Thursday, Aug. 6. Trying to gain momentum ahead of UAAP Season 89, the Fighting Maroons held their ground against the Beijing-based school with Veejay Pre leveling the match at 74-all off a right corner triple. However, the Chinese bets stormed back with a 7-0 blitz to create a 81-74 separation that they maintained up to the end. With its loss, UP was relegated to the classification round where it awaits its next rival. Meanwhile, Tsinghua University sets up a semis showdown against Shanghai Jiao Tong University. Noy Remogat starred for the Maroons with 19 points, four rebounds, and five assists, while Pre posted a double-double outing of 18 points and 12 rebounds on top of three assists and one block. Dieonte Miles contributed 10 points along with eight rebounds, three blocks, while Gani Stevens chipped in seven points and seven rebounds. James Payosing, for his part, listed four points, 10 rebounds, and four assists. Shi Kui steered Tsinghua with 26 points, five rebounds, and six assists, while Yu Haotian and Liu Qingwen added 15 and 10 points, respectively. Prior to their quarters loss, the Goldwin Monteverde-mentored crew finished with a 1-1 win-loss card in Group B, which was topped by Korea University (2-0), to earn its quarters ticket.

Centeno shrugs off match-fixing allegations after world 10-ball finals loss. Chezka Centeno made one thing clear: she simply had an off game. Centeno denied match-fixing accusations following her heartbreaking 4-1, 4-0, 1-4, 0-4, 4-0 loss to Margarita Fefilova of Belarus in the championship round of the 2026 WPA Women’s 10-Ball World Championship in Rome, Italy Thursday, Aug. 6. The 27-year-old Centeno, who fell short for a record-breaking third 10-ball title and settled for a silver medal in the elite 64-player women's field, took pride in reaching the final while brushing aside doubts over her championship-round performance. For the Zamboanga City native, who took the 8-Ball diadem last month, it was simply wasn't her day. “After seeing how widespread these accusations became, I felt this was something I had to address just once. I understand why some people are disappointed with the outcome, but everyone has off matches,” said Centeno. “I've seen the match-fixing accusations circulating in some Filipino comment sections, and while I know they don't represent everyone, those claims are simply not true. Miscues and mistakes happen, even at the highest level. That's the reality of sports,” she added. Centeno stressed that her sole focus was defending her crown while graciously acknowledging eventual champion Fefilova for her impressive performance. “I stepped to the table with one goal: to defend my title. Unfortunately, things didn't go my way, and my mistakes cost me the match. That's part of competition, no matter how difficult it is to accept,” Centeno continued. “That said, I'll move forward, just as I always have. Most importantly, Margarita played a great match, earned the championship, and deserves every bit of the credit. Congratulations, Margarita Fefilova Styer,” she concluded. Centeno bagged the silver medal and the bridesmaid’s purse of $33,000 (around P2 million), while champion Fefilova took home $55,000 (P3.3 million). Before suffering a finals defeat, the two-time world 10-ball winner got the better of South Korean Seao Seo, 4-0, 4-3, 4-3, in the semis, while dealing Japan’s Chihiro Kawahara a 4-3, 4-1, 3-4, 4-0 quarters loss. It was an impressive comeback for Centeno despite dropping her second game off a 3-4, 4-2, 2-4 loss to her friend and fellow Filipina champion Rubilen Amit, who was eliminated in the quarters, resulting in her being relegated to the losers’ bracket. There, Centeno managed to win three more games to keep her contention alive by advancing to the Last 16 where she dispatched American Savannah Easton, 4-1, 2-4, 4-0, 4-1.

Eala, William reunion cut short as pair suffers first-round loss in Toronto. The much-awaited reunion between Alex Eala and tennis icon Venus Williams was cut short after suffering a 4-6, 3-6 loss to Miyu Kato and Liudmila Samsonova in the opening round of the WTA 1000 National Bank Open doubles event in Toronto, Canada Friday, Aug. 7 (Philippine time). Still feeling the effects of her previous singles match in Toronto, the 21-year-old Eala dug deep to help the former world No. 1 erase a 2-4 deficit and level the opening set at 4-4, drawing cheers from the packed crowd at Sobeys Stadium. However, the Japanese-Russian pair regained control as they stormed back by winning the next two games to snatch the opening frame. Eala and Williams, unfortunately, fell to a 4-0 hole in the second set, and, despite mounting a fiery comeback, still found no answers to defuse Kato and Samsonova who made sure to secure their Round of 16 ticket. Kato and Samsonova now battle either No. 3 seed Sara Errani and Nicole Melichar-Martinez or the tandem of Americans Jessica Pegula and McCartney Kessler in the Last 16. Eala and Williams, meanwhile, bowed out of the doubles event in their reunion as partners. It can be remembered that Eala and Williams withdrew from the WTA 500 D.C. Open doubles tournament , with the former eventually capturing the singles crown. Their first partnership took place in the Bad Homburg Open in Germany, where Eala and Williams had a winning debut against Alexandra Osborne and Catherine Harrison, 6-3, 6-4, in the opener, before yielding a 3-6, 2-6 second-round result to Tereza Mihalikova of Slovakia and Olivia Nicholls of Great Britain.

Nickel Asia power unit rebrands as clean energy pipeline grows. Nickel Asia Corp. (NAC) is expanding its renewable power footprint with plans to build an additional 374 megawatt-peaks of solar projects, following its unit rebranding aimed at broadening the mining company’s push into clean energy. In a statement on Friday, Aug. 7, NAC announced that the listed nickel producer transformed its energy subsidiary, formerly known as Emerging Power Inc., into NAC Energy Inc. to align the unit with the parent firm. The rebrand comes as NAC Energy builds on its existing 293 megawatt-peaks of operating capacity as of July 2026. NAC Energy’s active development pipeline includes the 120-megawatt-peak Phase 2 of the San Isidro Solar Power Corp. project in Leyte, the 145-megawatt-peak Subic Solar Project in Zambales, the 50-megawatt-peak Nazareno Solar Project in Bataan, and the 59-megawatt-peak Botolan Solar Project in Zambales. “This rebranding is far more than a name change—it is a clear statement of who we are today and where we are heading,” Martin Antonio G. Zamora, president and chief executive officer of NAC Energy, said in the statement. “We are no longer just an emerging player; we have proven our capacity to execute, scale, and deliver reliable power,” he added. Zamora noted that bringing the unit under the corporate brand reinforces the conglomerate’s goal to transition toward a sustainable natural resource and clean energy platform through 2030, reducing its reliance solely on traditional mining assets. In addition to expanding its solar pipeline, NAC Energy plans to branch into flexible baseload and mid-merit power generation to help stabilize the country’s electricity grid, with a specific focus on off-grid and island regions facing energy security challenges. “Our non-negotiable standard is simple: to deliver secure and cheaper power to the Filipino people without sacrificing our sustainability imperatives,” Zamora said. “Clean energy must walk hand-in-hand with energy security and accessibility.” Nickel Asia operates seven nickel mines in the Philippines and holds a 10 percent equity stake in the Taganito High Pressure Acid Leach plant. (Gabriell Christel Galang)

Lights, mics, nominations: Awit Awards 2026 contenders revealed. Philippine music's awards season has officially begun, bringing with it the annual celebration of the industry's biggest hits, breakthrough artists and creative achievements — along with the inevitable debates over who made the cut and who was left out. The organizers of the 39th Awit Awards on Friday unveiled this year's nominees, with chart-toppers, OPM mainstays and rising acts competing across dozens of categories in what is widely regarded as the Philippine music industry's equivalent of the Grammy Awards. Among the contenders for the night's top honor, Album of the Year, are Cup of Joe's "Silakbo," SB19's "DAM," Ben&Ben's "Saranggola," IV of Spades' "Konsensya," and Dionela featuring Loonie's "Ikigai." For Song of the Year, the nominees include IV of Spades' "Aura," Fitterkarma's "Pag-Ibig Ay Kanibalismo II," SB19's "DUNGKA!," IV of Spades' "Kabisado," Maki's "Kahel Na Langit," and Dionela and Loonie's "Ikigai." The race for Best New Artist features Gab Cabangon, New Lore, VVINK and DJ Love featuring Pio Balbuena, Jamiela, and It All Started in May. Behind the scenes, Brian Lotho, Shadiel Chan, John Paulo Nase, Joshua Daniel Nase and Tim Dionela are among the nominees for Producer of the Year, while John Paulo Nase, Joshua Daniel Nase, Blaster Silonga, Daniel Zildjian Benitez, Tim Dionela, Lola Amour, Joao De Leon and Marlon Peroramas are competing for Songwriter of the Year. In the performance categories, Janine Berdin, Maki, Noel Cabangon, dwta, Rico Blanco, Rob Deniel and Jay R are nominated for Best Performance by a Solo Artist. Best Collaboration Performance includes Sarah Geronimo and SB19's "Umaaligid," One Click Straight and Clara Benin's "Telepono," Jason Dhakal and Oliver Cronin, BINI featuring Agnez Mo's "Blink Twice," Lola Amour and KOKORO of PSYCHIC FEVER from EXILE TRIBE's "The Moment," and ZIV with Jolianne's "Kuryente." SB19 also landed nominations for "DUNGKA!" in Best Dance/Electronic Recording and for its music videos, while IV of Spades, Dionela, Cup of Joe, Maki and Ben&Ben earned multiple nominations across the grand, performance and technical award categories. The Awit Awards, presented annually by the Philippine Association of the Record Industry (PARI), recognize excellence in recorded music and honor achievements in artistry, songwriting, production and technical craftsmanship across the Philippine music industry.

US, Japan retain ‘good’ trust rating among Filipinos — SWS. The United States and Japan received good trust ratings from Filipinos, while China, Palestine, and Iran continued to receive poor trust ratings in the latest Social Weather Stations (SWS) survey. The Second Quarter 2026 Social Weather Survey, conducted from June 20 to 29, found the United States posting a “good” net trust rating of +42, followed by Japan at +36. Australia received a “moderate” +29, while Israel (-5) and Russia (-8) were rated “neutral.” China (-16), Palestine (-19), and Iran (-23) remained in the “poor” category. SWS said the United States’ rating improved by three points from +39 in March to +42 in June. Japan’s rating also climbed from +34 to +36, while Australia's rating improved from +23 to +29. Israel's rating slipped from +1 to -5, while Russia's net trust score declined from -5 to -8. Meanwhile, China's rating improved slightly from -19 to -16. Palestine's net trust rating dropped from -12 to -19, while Iran's score edged down from -22 to -23. The survey was conducted through face-to-face interviews with 1,200 adults nationwide. It had sampling error margins of ±3 percentage points for national estimates and ±6 percentage points for each of Metro Manila, Balance Luzon, the Visayas, and Mindanao.

HCLTech strengthens its Philippines presence, championing Filipino talent for global digital services. We believe that every employee can find their spark as long as we empower them to discover their passions, unlock their potential and shape the future of technology,” added Amrita Das, Head HR, Growth Markets (APAC), HCLTech. As demand for digital transformation accelerates, the company remains focused on strengthening its capabilities in digital workplace services, business services and next-generation technologies.
