Why memorable photos are usually taken from farther away, according to Xiaomi. Most people reach for a smartphone's telephoto camera to pull a faraway subject closer. Concerts, stages, the moon. That instinct is correct, but it misses the more useful half of what a long lens does, especially for anyone learning to tell stories with their phone rather than simply take pictures. Many of today's strongest visual storytellers, from veteran photographers to creators just building their following online, share one discipline: They understand that a camera changes the moment it points at the subject. Announce "Picture!" and the room rearranges itself—the scene that made you reach for your phone in the first place gives way to a performance staged for it. Here is how the Xiaomi 17T Series and Xiaomi 17 Series help preserve authentic moments through three storytelling habits: keeping your distance, giving the moment time, and preserving the atmosphere that makes it memorable. 1. Framing and distance: let the lens do the approaching Composition guides where the eye goes, and the single biggest composition decision most people never think about is where they stand. Step toward a candid moment and you break it. Stay put and let the telephoto cross the room instead of your feet, and the moment survives intact. This is the real argument for the Xiaomi 17T Series' Leica 5x Telephoto camera, which offers the reach of a classic 115mm lens with optical stabilization. From the hallway, your subject stays absorbed in what they are doing. From across a barangay court, a game keeps its scale and its honesty. The lens does the approaching so that you never have to. There is another reason telephoto photos often feel more intentional. Their longer focal lengths naturally simplify busy backgrounds, so a single face separates cleanly from the tarpaulins and string lights behind it, letting the people and the story stand out. That subject-isolation look is a large part of what reads as "professional." Try this: Pick a subject doing something absorbing, like your grandparents sharing a quiet moment over morning coffee. Stay just far enough back that you don't interrupt what they're doing, then let the telephoto fill the frame. You'll be surprised how naturally the story, and the composition, come together. 2. Timing and emotion: photograph people before they perform Great storytelling is often less about where you stand than when you press the shutter. The moment someone hears "Picture!" conversations pause, smiles stiffen, and genuine expressions become practiced ones. Sometimes the best photograph happens just before that announcement, or right after everyone forgets about posing and returns to the moment. This is where the Leica 5x Telephoto becomes more than a zoom lens. By letting you keep a respectful distance without sacrificing composition, it gives everyday moments the space to unfold naturally while you wait for the right expression, gesture, or glance. You are no longer directing the scene—you are observing it with patience. Try this: Find someone absorbed in what they're doing, whether it's a street musician performing, a barista crafting a latte, or a friend sketching in a café. Let the Leica 5x Telephoto do the approaching while you stay where you are. Resist the urge to press the shutter immediately. Sometimes the best frame comes just before the subject acknowledges you. Other times, it comes in the very instant they do, with an unrehearsed laugh, an amused eye roll, a bashful grin, or a smile that's genuine precisely because it wasn't planned. 3. Let the evening stay evening The stories worth keeping don't stop when the sun goes down. They continue over late dinners, conversations that stretch long after dessert, and moments shared under the warm glow of a single pendant light. The challenge isn't making these scenes brighter, it’s preserving the atmosphere. The Xiaomi 17 Series is built for exactly that. Its Leica Summilux lens opens to a wide ƒ/1.67 aperture and feeds a Light Fusion 950 sensor designed to capture more light and preserve a wide dynamic range. Instead of turning evening into artificial daylight, it keeps warm indoor lighting looking warm, allowing the mood of the moment to remain intact. Whether you're photographing from across the dining room or observing from the doorway, the same storytelling principle applies: preserve the scene without interrupting it, and let the light tell its part of the story. Try this: After sunset, leave the flash off and resist maxing the brightness. Let the room's existing warm light lead, expose for the faces, and keep the shadows where they fall. The photo will remember the evening the way it actually felt. Turning single shots into stories One strong frame is a photo. A handful of related frames tells a story. Think in beginnings, middles, and endings: preparation, action, reaction. A family meal from the first chopped onion to the last cleared plate. A child learning something new, from the first failed attempt to the moment it finally clicks. Build a small series around a single afternoon or theme and share it as a carousel or an album rather than a lone post. A series invites people back into the experience in a way a single image cannot. The Xiaomi 17T Series and Xiaomi 17 Series don't create these moments. They simply make them easier to preserve. The Leica 5x Telephoto lets you step back without sacrificing intimacy, while the Xiaomi 17 Series' advanced low-light imaging helps preserve the atmosphere after sunset. Together they support the habit that separates snapshots from stories: photograph life as it is already happening, and let people keep being themselves.

Bam Aquino: New law gives DepEd flexibility to determine approach to K-12 curriculum. Senator Paolo “Bam” Aquino IV welcomed the new law that amended certain provisions of the Enhanced Basic Education Act, removing the mandatory requirement to use the spiral progression approach in the K to 12 curriculum. This after Republic Act No. 12322, which Aquino principally sponsored and co-authored as chairperson of the Senate Committee on Basic Education, lapsed into law on Aug. 2. RA 12322 specifically amends Section 5 of Republic Act No. 10533, or the Enhanced Basic Education Act of 2013, giving the Department of Education (DepEd) greater flexibility to adopt the teaching approach it deems most effective, subject to periodic review. This marks Aquino's second education measure enacted in the 20th Congress, following the passage of Republic Act No. 12321, or the Last Mile and Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas (GIDA) Schools Act. “Under this law, the spiral progression approach will be removed to give DepEd the flexibility to choose the most effective teaching methods for our students,” Aquino said. “This is a crucial step toward resolving the education crisis and will help improve proficiency and literacy in our schools,” he stressed. Moreover, Aquino said the measure will help ensure students achieve the necessary mastery before advancing to the next grade level. During his sponsorship speech on the measure, Aquino noted that his consultations with teachers showed that the mandatory implementation of the spiral progression methodology has made teaching and learning more difficult. Even the Year One Report of the Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM 2) found that the mandatory spiral progression approach posted practical difficulties for teachers in delivering the curriculum as intended which also affected how students build knowledge and skills effectively across grade levels. According to the report, the framework also forced teachers to teach multiple discipline instead of specializing in their areas of expertise, particularly in Science and Mathematics, resulting in congested lessons and weaker mastery of foundational concepts.

Bill expanding government's options for socialized housing hurdles House. A measure that seeks to expands the land, financing, and partnership options available for socialized housing projects was overwhelmingly passed on third and final reading in the House of Representatives. Approved on the strength of 205 "yes" votes as opposed to only three "no" votes during plenary session Wednesday, Aug. 5 was House Bill (HB) No. 9697, House Majority Leader Ilocos Norte 1st district Rep. Sandro Marcos said. No abstentions were recorded during nominal voting among the congressmen. According to Rep. Marcos, HB No. 9697 seeks to improve the delivery of socialized housing programs by amending Sections 10, 18, and 20 of Republic Act (RA) No. 7279, or the Urban Development and Housing Act of 1992, as amended by RA No. 10884, or the Balanced Housing Development Program Amendments. The presidential son said the measure would help the government turn more idle, foreclosed and underused properties into secure communities for Filipinos who need housing most. “President Ferdinand ‘Bongbong’ R. Marcos Jr. has made housing a central part of his development agenda, and Speaker Bojie Dy has ensured that the House responds with legislation that can actually move projects from paper to construction. HB No. 9697 gives government and the private sector more workable routes to provide ordinary families with safe, dignified and affordable homes,” Rep. Marcos noted. If enacted, the bill would amend key provisions of RA No. 7279, or the Urban Development and Housing Act of 1992, to improve the delivery of socialized housing programs. The bill expands the methods for acquiring land and creating housing projects to include community mortgages, land swapping, land consolidation, land banking, donations, joint ventures, negotiated purchases, direct purchases and unsolicited proposals under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Code. Government-owned and foreclosed properties may be acquired by local governments, the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD) and national housing agencies primarily through negotiated purchase. Properties forfeited because of unpaid real property taxes would be prioritized for socialized housing, while qualified beneficiaries already occupying the land would receive the right of first refusal. Subdivision developers would be required to provide socialized housing equivalent to at least 15 percent of the total project area or project cost, while condominium and vertical housing developers would comply at a rate of at least 5 percent. Developers may satisfy the requirement through new settlements, joint ventures, community mortgage projects or payments dedicated to housing programs in the city or municipality where the private project is located. The resulting housing projects would prioritize informal settler families, underprivileged and homeless citizens and residents displaced by major infrastructure projects. Local governments would receive a two-year exclusive period to use payments made by developers for their own socialized housing programs, subject to extensions during disasters, calamities and other extraordinary circumstances. HB No.9697 also provides for one-stop shops, simplified accreditation and the issuance of complete permits, licenses and clearances within 90 days, while extending qualified tax incentives to participating socialized housing projects. “We are making housing policy more responsive to the realities faced by our communities. Hindi sapat ang housing target kung mabagal ang permits, kulang ang lupa at walang malinaw na paraan para magtulungan ang national government, LGUs at private developers,” said the majority leader. (The housing target is not enough if permits are slow, land is lacking, and there is no clear way for the national government, LGUs, and private developers to work together.) The measure also increases penalties for violations, directs collected fines to socialized housing in the affected locality and requires the DHSUD to issue implementing rules within 90 days and submit an evaluation and accomplishment report to Congress.

NPD nabs 2 cops in Caloocan over alleged illegal firearms sale. Operatives of the Northern Police District (NPD) arrested two active police officers assigned to the Caloocan City Police Station (CCPS) in a buy-bust operation over the alleged illegal sale of firearms in Caloocan City. The operation was conducted on Thursday, August 6, at around 5:30 a.m., along Riles Compound in Barangay 5, Caloocan City, with support from the CCPS Intelligence Unit, Intelligence and Detective Management Section (IDMS), and several police sub-stations. Police said the suspects were arrested after allegedly completing the sale of firearms to a civilian poseur-buyer. Seized from the suspects were two Philippine National Police-issued 9mm pistols, a .38-caliber revolver, a 12-gauge shotgun, several magazines and rounds of live ammunition, marked buy-bust money, two cellular phones, and two motorcycles. The confiscated firearms will undergo ballistic examination to determine whether they were used in previous shooting incidents. Investigators will also trace the ownership and origin of the recovered weapons. The two officers will face charges for alleged violations of Sections 28 and 29 of Republic Act No. 10591, or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act. NPD Acting District Director Brig. Gen. Benliner Capili said the incident should serve as a warning to police commanders and supervisors to remain vigilant against personnel who may become involved in illegal activities. “This incident should serve as an eye opener to all of us – that the vulnerability/possibility of our personnel to engage in illegal activities is very high if we will put our guards down,” Capili said. He also reminded chiefs of police and unit commanders to strengthen counterintelligence efforts and other interventions to prevent similar incidents that could tarnish the image of the NPD and police stations in the Camanava area. “Personnel committing the same offense shall face maximum administrative sanction, while their immediate superior or supervisor shall be held accountable under the Doctrine of Command Responsibility,” Capili said. Administrative cases will also be filed against the two police officers as the investigation continues.

‘Irresponsible and disrespectful’: DFA condemns caskets bearing anti-Chinese message, vows accountability. Stressing that threats or acts of violence against any individual, including foreign nationals and government officials, are unacceptable, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Friday, Aug. 7, strongly condemned the display of caskets bearing an anti-Chinese message . In a statement, the DFA said it "does not condone acts or threats of violence against any individual, including foreign nationals or officials." "Such irresponsible and disrespectful acts cannot be tolerated," the DFA said. Freedom of expression has limits, DFA says While recognizing the constitutional right to freedom of expression, the DFA emphasized that this right does not extend to threats of violence or actions that endanger the safety and security of others. The department said such acts are inconsistent with the Philippine government's conduct of foreign relations and do not represent how Filipinos express criticism or dissatisfaction, even on sensitive political issues. "While the Philippines upholds the right to freedom of expression, the DFA emphasizes that this right does not extend to threats of violence or acts that endanger the safety and security of others," it said. The DFA added that these actions "do not reflect the Philippine government's approach to conducting its foreign relations, nor do they represent how Filipinos express criticism or dissatisfaction, even on sensitive political matters." Reaffirms commitment to protect foreign nationals The DFA also reiterated the Philippine government's commitment to ensuring the safety and security of foreign nationals and officials in the country. "The Philippine government reaffirms that it takes seriously its duties and obligations concerning the safety and security of foreign nationals and officials in the country," the DFA said. It noted that the Philippines continues to fulfill its obligations under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations and the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, which require host states to protect diplomatic and consular personnel. Investigation underway The DFA said it is coordinating closely with law enforcement authorities, which are investigating the incident to determine the circumstances surrounding the display of the caskets and identify those responsible. "The DFA is closely coordinating with law enforcement authorities, which are taking the necessary steps to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and determine accountability for this reckless act," the department said.

A taste of New York begins at Fil-Am chef Suzanne Cupps' Lola's. New York City will always mean different things for a returning, visiting Filipino. My last time in Manhattan was two years ago, but that was in early March, for work, during a cold late-winter spell. This time it was glorious summer in late July, and for me, New York is primarily about the theater, the food and dining, the museums, and making new memories. Filipinos are traditionally creatures of habit. Do you notice how when we visit Hong Kong, we’ll end up eating in the very same places we enjoyed in the past? It was tempting to head back to Peter Luger in Brooklyn for a steak dinner, and gravitate to Levain Bakery for their cookies, but we made the promise to try new dining places, explore the city, and carve out new "go-to's." So if you’re heading to Manhattan later in the year, feel free to head to any of the eating establishments and shows mentioned below. I’m picking out the best of our seven days there, and hope you’ll enjoy them as much as we did! To make it easy, I’m also breaking them down into dinner and fine-dining places, current Broadway shows worth catching, casual brunch and lunch options, bakeries and dessert choices, and cultural and museum spots. And I’m breaking the recommendations into Parts 1 and 2 to lessen possible information overload. La Mercerie: Located on the corner of Mercer and Canal in Soho, La Mercerie is a French-inspired dining spot that’s conjoined to an interior design store, the Roman and Williams Guild, so you can imagine what the ambiance and table settings here are like. I had the Sole de Paris, which was their novel take on Sole Meunière, but served with button mushrooms and a white wine sauce. This was the perfect light dinner I had aspired for. Issa ordered the Navarin D’Agneau, a lamb stew, with English peas, carrots, turnips, and asparagus. It was a hearty serving despite the size of the bowl, and Issa smartly asked that she take home what she couldn’t finish, and it was her breakfast the next morning. Her dessert was the superb Hazelnut Pecan Cake, and I’m told their chocolate chip cookie is to die for. Lola’s: This is the bastion of chef Suzanne Cupps, who, with partner Nick Salinger, has made Lola’s cited for two years in a row in The New York Times 100 Best Restaurants in NYC. And the reason I lead this feature with chef Suzanne is because she’s proudly half-Filipina. Her dad is Cesar Paraiso, and the Lola her restaurant is named after is Cesar’s mother. Her distinctly Filipino wedding photo is found by the restaurant’s bar. Vegetable-forward, and influenced by her Filipino, Asian, and South Carolina upbringing, there’s a wonderful inventiveness to the Lola’s menu. And it’s centrally located on W. 28th Street and Fifth Avenue, just across the 28th Street entrance of the Fifth Avenue Hotel. Her Crispy Chicken Thighs are accompanied by "suka," and you’ll love the waiter trying to pronounce "suka." We really loved the dishes here, and how among the zero-proof drinks, you’ll find a Suman Soda. It’s not Filipino cuisine per se, but just great food stamped with chef Suzanne’s own provenance and culinary history. Visit Lola’s and say hello to chef Suzanne, and ask if her Leche Flan is available that day. Broadway shows 'Schmigadoon': Taking home four Tony Awards in total this 2026, this is the Best Musical of the year, and you’ll immediately see why it won these awards. The acting, the singing, the dancing are all impeccable; the humor and laughter are non-stop, and the second act is just as strong as the first! In previous visits to New York, that was my personal gripe: how shows like "Hamilton" and even "The Book of Mormon" would start so strong, but flag in the second act, and I’d be wishing they’d come to the end of the book. If you have a single funny bone in your body, trust me and watch this crazy, heartfelt parody and tribute to Broadway musicals of the past. 'Stranger Things: The First Shadow': I was probably the only member of the audience who had never watched an episode of this limited series. But with Issa as spirit guide, I quickly got into this and appreciated how the stage design and special effects were so special, creating chilling suspense and drama as needed. It was a perfectly staged version of the TV show, and acted as a prequel that drew much appreciation from the audience. I understand one of the shows will be filmed to act as a Netflix special. Me, I was just transfixed and enjoyed it, so can imagine how that would be heightened if you or your children are fans. For casual dining Bubby’s: On Hudson Street in Tribeca, Bubby’s delivers classic, from-scratch American comfort food. It’s been around since the 1990s, and on the Monday morning, at 11:20, that we walked to Bubby’s, there was already a long line of people waiting to get a table. It’s most famous for its James Beard fluffy buttermilk pancakes. And be sure to try their Crab Cake Benedict, and seasonal desserts. I was told the lines got even more dense after the JFK Jr. and Carolyn series aired last year, as this was their staple neighborhood hangout, since they lived just up the block. As it’s in Tribeca, where major local film offices are found, expect that crowd to regularly show up. 'Los Tacos No. 1 at Chelsea Market': A trip to Chelsea Market, W. 15th Street and Ninth Avenue, will always be a good idea when looking for affordable quality eats. It’s like what you’ll find in the Mercato in Florence, and what our own Mercato aspires to be. And when at Chelsea Market, expect the longest line to be at Los Tacos No. 1. My tip? The Chicken Quesadillas and the Taco Adobada, and choose the corn tortillas. For dessert and baked treats Dominique Ansel Bakery: Issa had gotten wind of a Pierre Hermé-Dominique Ansel collaboration, so we were there, waiting in line, before the shop even opened on a Thursday morning. Hermé is known worldwide for his intense, exotically flavored macarons, and Issa has been an ardent fan for a decade now. Ansel is credited with coming up with the first Cronut. So this was "dessert heaven pairing" as far as pastry fans were concerned. On Spring Street, in Soho. The three special desserts of the collaboration were a flan, a biscuit, and a cronut. The chocolate flan was my favorite, and gets its photo highlighted. Also order Ansel’s Key Lime Pie éclair. Ansel also has a French-Asian bread place called Papa D’Amour (64 University Place, near NYU); Asian because his wife is from Taiwan. Worth checking out, and he said to try their egg tart. Culture Espresso: I’m not a coffee person, so I dropped by this place just to get their chocolate chip cookie. Also ordered the corn cookie, and their oatmeal cranberry. It’s a favorite on social media, and I get it, as it’s crisp on the very first bite and edges, then becomes soft and gooey in the center. They’ve got this technique down pat, and I experienced this on all three cookie variants. I still prefer Levain, but could appreciate how this one is different and still good. There are several Culture Espresso locations all over the city. For Days at the museum Banksy Museum: On the corner of Canal and Broadway, this is really a tribute museum, an act of love from the fans of the anonymous graffiti street artist. The tour takes you from the very beginning of Banksy’s career in Bristol, and takes us through the 1990s, up to his more recent escapades in Ukraine and in London. His incendiary political work is cataloged and reproduced on the walls of this museum. So that’s my first batch of recommendations, a mix of the highbrow and the ones with street cred. And for me, that’s the beauty of New York. It’s a (big) apple that can be sliced, diced, picked at, or nibbled. The important thing is to enjoy your time there, and come away with lasting experiences.

Authorities probe caskets with anti-China, anti-rebel banners in Metro Manila. At least five caskets carrying anti-China and anti-Communist Party of the Philippines-New People’s Army (CPP-NPA) messages were left in separate locations in Metro Manila, prompting an investigation on Friday, Aug. 7. The caskets were found in Sta. Cruz, Manila; Barangay 54 in Caloocan City; Barangay South Triangle and Barangay Sta. Teresita in Quezon City; and along Gil Puyat Avenue in Makati City. Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr., chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP), ordered a comprehensive probe to establish the facts and circumstances behind the incidents. "The Philippine National Police (PNP) is aware of the circulating videos and social media posts regarding abandoned caskets reportedly found in different parts of Metro Manila," Nartatez said. "The concerned police units are validating each reported incident and are coordinating with the respective local government units and other appropriate agencies to determine the circumstances surrounding the recovery of the caskets. The recovered caskets, together with other materials found at the scene, have been secured as part of the investigation to establish their origin, purpose, and whether any laws or local ordinances may have been violated," he added. The National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) said its initial investigation showed that the caskets were deliberately abandoned by masked individuals aboard white and gray vans between 2 and 4 a.m. on Aug. 7. “These caskets contained anti-CPP-NPA and anti-China messages,” the NCRPO said, adding that the incidents appeared designed to stir public reaction. The discovery in several areas within a few hours prompted police units to secure the sites and examine the items. The incidents also drew attention because of the political messages attached to the caskets. The Quezon City Police District (QCPD) said responding officers secured the areas and inspected the caskets. Both were found to contain only crumpled papers. The banners attached to them carried the messages, “CHINESE COMMUNIST PARTY (CCP) GREEDY! SALOT” and “GREEDY SALOT.” Another casket bore pictures of two unidentified individuals. Police have since taken the caskets into police custody for further examination and formed a Special Investigation Team to identify those responsible, determine the motive, and trace the vehicles used. “NCRPO is treating these incidents as deliberate acts intended to attract attention, provoke public reaction, and possibly create unnecessary alarm,” it said. NCRPO investigators were deployed to conduct backtracking and forward tracking of closed-circuit television footage. The police regional office also directed units across Metro Manila to strengthen vigilance and prevent similar incidents while the investigation continues. “Public safety cannot be used as a stage for fear,” the NCRPO said. It urged the public to remain calm and avoid circulating unverified information. Residents were also told to report suspicious activity or information to the nearest police station. “This cowardly act will not be left unpunished. NCRPO will ensure that the identity of those who are behind these acts will be uncovered and criminal cases will be filed upon completion of the investigation,” the NCRPO said.

Former Ginebra players mourn passing of longtime Kings utility man Ian Calilan. Former Barangay Ginebra players paid tribute to Kings longtime utility man Christianne "Ian" Calilan, who passed away on Wednesday, Aug. 5, following a lingering illness. He was 51. Calilan had been a part of the Kings franchise since joining the team's utility staff in 1999 and he was still with the team during Ginebra's game against Magnolia on Sunday, Aug. 2. He also came from a well-known basketball family, with his father, Cris Calilan, having been a member of the legendary 1976 Crispa grand slam team and grandfather Francisco "Kiko" Calilan who was part of the men’s national team that won the country’s first basketball gold in the Asian Games in 1951. The news of his passing prompted an outpouring of sympathy from the Ginebra community, with players, coaches and staff rallying to extend support to Calilan's family. Among those who paid tribute were former Ginebra stars Jayjay Helterbrand and Jared Dillinger, both of whom shared heartfelt messages on social media. "For more than two decades, Ian faithfully served the team as its dedicated ball boy and utility staff, becoming a familiar and cherished presence since joining the franchise in 1999. More than his role, he was family to many within the organization," Helterbrand wrote on his official Facebook page. "Among those who shared a bond with Ian was Jayjay Helterbrand. Through countless games, victories, and unforgettable moments, their bond reflected the strong family culture that has always defined Barangay Ginebra," he added. Dillinger also expressed disbelief over Calilan's passing. "I still can't believe you're gone brother," he wrote. "As we get older, we realize that life has a painful way of taking people and moments away from us. Learning how to carry that loss is one of the hardest parts of life, something none of us are ever truly prepared for." "We're going to miss you, Ian. I'm grateful we became so close during those bubble championship days. I miss you already, my man," he added.

Palace sees economy recovering in second half after 2.3% GDP growth. Malacañang expects the Philippine economy to regain momentum in the second half of the year after growth slowed to 2.3 percent in the second quarter, with the government moving to accelerate spending and infrastructure projects. Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro acknowledged that the latest growth figure was below the government's expectations but maintained that the slowdown would be temporary. “We acknowledge that the country's economic growth in the second quarter was 2.3 percent. This result was lower than we had hoped,” Castro said Friday, Aug. 7. “The numbers show the challenges we have faced, but they do not determine the country’s long-term direction. This slowdown is only temporary,” she added. Castro said the government expects economic activity to improve as it speeds up spending and the release of budgets in the coming months. “As the government continues to speed up spending and release budgets more quickly, we hope the economy can start to pick up in the second half of the year as well,” she said. Middle East conflict, construction slowdown The Palace Press Officer attributed the slowdown to unusual events, particularly the impact of the Middle East conflict on inflation, fuel prices, employment, and remittances, as well as weaker public construction. Castro said the slowdown in public construction was temporary as the government intensified efforts to address corruption in infrastructure spending. The administration plans to fast-track high-impact infrastructure projects, maintain price stability, and continue targeted assistance for vulnerable sectors as part of efforts to accelerate growth in the second half. Among the interventions cited by Castro were expanded UPLIFT assistance covering 7.5 million families, the P12-per-liter Fuel Subsidy Program, and the Bawat Bayan Makikinabang Rice Program. Exports, manufacturing show resilience Despite weaker overall economic growth, Castro said exports grew by 12.2 percent on strong demand for electronics and semiconductors, AI-related products, and agricultural goods, with merchandise exports posting double-digit growth for five consecutive quarters. Manufacturing expanded by 2.6 percent, while agriculture grew by 2.7 percent, and travel exports increased by 12.6 percent as tourism continued to recover. Castro said the administration would seek to further expand exports and improve competitiveness while positioning the Philippines to benefit from the global AI and digital economy through investments in skills, technology, and higher-value industries, including Pax Silica. Tax, power measures for middle class The Palace also cited priority Legislative-Executive Development Advisory Council (LEDAC) measures aimed at supporting the middle class and household consumption, including proposals to raise the personal income tax exemption threshold to P350,000 and abolish the travel tax. Other measures include proposed amendments to the Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA) to prohibit distribution utilities and electric cooperatives from passing system loss charges and the corresponding value-added tax to consumers, the Sariling Kuryente Act, a minimum corporate income tax exemption for small businesses, and a general tax amnesty.

Robbie Jaworski dreams of making his mark in action films. Robbie Jaworski made his showbiz debut in 2024. After appearing in the blockbuster film "Meet, Greet & Bye" to his series debut in "The Alibi", the son of Mikee Cojuangco and Robert “Dodot” Jaworski Jr. is now ready to explore a wider range of roles. "Pangarap ko in terms of acting, gusto kong sumali sa mga action, one day sana," Robbie said during a recent press conference. But he is not diving into it unprepared. "Sa ngayon siguro ang gusto kong gawin is I want to learn mga martial arts, or 'yung parkour, tapos 'yung mga action scenes pwedeng-pwede ko nang gawin 'yon," he said. His dream? Joining the cast of “Incognito.” "Siguro one dream project right now is makapasok ako sa 'Incognito'," he said, adding in jest, "Direk, pwede naman po akong mag-audition." Apart from acting, he is also busy as MYX VJ and as co-host of "Y Speak 2.0." Hosting "Y Speak 2.0" gives Robbie a different kind fulfillment. "Projects like 'Y Speak' na may substance siya, may maayos at magandang content ka na pinag-uusapan. So, I feel incredibly blessed to have the opportunities and the lessons that I've learned through my projects. Para sa akin kasi ang goal ko talaga sa buhay, whether sa showbiz o sa business or sa personal life, is gusto ko maging blessing sa ibang tao. Gusto kong maging isang halimbawa na hindi mo kailangang pumasok sa politika para gumawa ng (pagbabago) sa Pilipinas. That's my goal in my life. So I love projects like 'Y Speak' because it's exactly that; I feel like I'm fulfilling that goal by being part of that project," he said.

MTRCB opposes proposed ban on violent films, TV shows. The MTRCB has pushed back against proposals to ban movies and television programs with violent themes, saying stronger parental guidance and responsible content regulation are more effective than outright prohibition. In a statement released Aug. 5, the Movie and Television Review and Classification Board said it shares public concern over the possible effects of violent content on children and young viewers. However, the agency stressed that its mandate under Presidential Decree No. 1986 is to assign age-appropriate classifications while supporting the growth of the local film and television industry, not to impose blanket bans. The MTRCB said prohibiting films and TV programs solely because they depict violence could infringe on the constitutional right of Filipino creatives to freedom of expression and artistic creation. Instead, the board urged parents, educators and other stakeholders to play a more active role in supervising children and helping them understand the context of what they watch, whether on television, in cinemas or on social media. The agency also highlighted its Responsableng Panonood Program, which uses its PROTECT Framework to educate parents, teachers and local officials on responsible media consumption among children. The MTRCB said protecting minors from harmful content is a shared responsibility among government, parents, schools, media practitioners, digital influencers and the entertainment industry. It added that it continues to work with film and television stakeholders to promote responsible self-regulation while ensuring Filipino cultural values are respected. The board said it remains committed to striking a balance between safeguarding children and upholding freedom of expression in Philippine media.

DFA: Ayungin resupply arrangement requires no permission from China. The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Friday, Aug. 7, defended the government's provisional understanding governing resupply missions to BRP Sierra Madre in Ayungin Shoal, saying it neither requires the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) to seek permission from China nor allows the boarding and inspection of Philippine vessels. In a statement, DFA Spokesperson for Maritime Affairs Rogelio Villanueva Jr. said the arrangement was crafted to prevent incidents and miscalculations at sea while ensuring the uninterrupted delivery of supplies and personnel to the grounded naval outpost. "The Provisional Understanding is intended to avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation at sea, does not require the AFP to seek permission, nor involve the boarding and inspection of its vessels during RORE missions," Villanueva said. He stressed that the DFA "will always uphold the country's sovereign rights in its exclusive economic zone (EEZ), as affirmed by the 2016 Arbitral Award." Arrangement protects Philippine rights The statement came in response to criticism from former Supreme Court Associate Justice Antonio Carpio, who questioned the government's handling of resupply operations in the West Philippine Sea. Earlier, Carpio warned that the DFA's provisional understanding with China regarding resupply missions to Ayungin Shoal could erode the Philippines' rights under the 2016 Arbitral Award. He also strongly opposed expanding the arrangement across the broader West Philippine Sea. Carpio urged to propose alternative However, Villanueva urged Carpio to propose a workable alternative that would allow the military to continue carrying out its missions safely and efficiently. "Instead of criticizing government actions, we invite former SC Associate Justice Antonio Carpio to offer the AFP any viable alternative that can ensure the continued efficient, timely, and safe conduct of resupply missions that provide essential supplies and facilitate the regular rotation of our troops aboard BRP Sierra Madre," he said. The DFA maintained that the provisional understanding supports the continued conduct of regular rotation and resupply (RORE) missions while protecting Philippine personnel stationed aboard BRP Sierra Madre, which serves as the country's military outpost in Ayungin Shoal. The department reiterated that the Philippines remains committed to defending its lawful rights and maritime entitlements in the West Philippine Sea, consistent with the landmark 2016 Arbitral Award, which invalidated China's sweeping claims under its so-called nine-dash line.

Kris Aquino returns with first project amid ongoing health battle. After years largely away from the spotlight while undergoing treatment for multiple autoimmune illnesses, Kris Aquino has taken on her first new project. The longtime television host and actress, known as the "Queen of All Media," was unveiled by Netflix as its new "C.H.I.K.A." or Chief Head of Insights and Kontent Analysis, in a promotional campaign released this week. In the lighthearted video, Aquino returns to one of the roles that made her a household name: offering candid, unfiltered opinions. Sitting beside editor Earljohn, she reviews scenes from three Filipino titles and shares her trademark commentary on what could be improved. Following Aquino's suggestions, scenes from "A Secret in Prague," "Blood vs Duty" and "The Master Cutter" are reworked with new effects and filters, transforming what she jokingly describes as "nakakaloka" moments into scenes she declares "love, love, love." While the appearance is promotional, it is Aquino's first project since stepping back from regular television work because of her health. Aquino has spent the past several years undergoing treatment in the United States and the Philippines for a series of autoimmune diseases. She has publicly disclosed diagnoses that include chronic spontaneous urticaria, autoimmune thyroid disease, eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), and systemic sclerosis, among other autoimmune conditions that have severely affected her immune system.

Gilas Women can be ‘top tier’, says new coach BT Toews. Newly-minted Gilas Pilipinas women’s team head coach Burke "BT" Toews is seeing so much potential in the national team, noting that the Nationals can get into top-tier level and be considered as one of the perennial contenders in Asia. Speaking during a media availability on Thursday, Aug. 6, Toews shared his thoughts about the women’s national team after already spending some practice time with the girls as part of their preparation for a loaded schedule through the next two months. Gilas is scheduled to play in the FIBA Women’s Olympic Pre-Qualifying Tournament in Guadalajara, Mexico from Aug. 19 to 23 before setting its sights on the Asian Games gold next month. “Of all the teams that I thought about — and I've had some other offers in Asia to coach national teams — I thought that the Philippines, the women's, were a team that had a really high ceiling,” said Toews, who left his Japanese team Fujitsu Red Wave where he won two championships with to coach Gilas. “Not just because of what happened in the last few years with Coach Pat (Aquino) and the success they had. But if things could be changed, not just on the court, but off the court, I thought that the Philippines could really get to the top tier and be a perennial contender," he explained. Toews is keen on applying the same blueprint that led the Red Wave to five finals appearances, back-to-back WJBL league titles (2024, 2025) and Empress Cup (All-Japan) crowns, while also utilizing and developing Gilas’ current strengths. "I will use my team more as a blueprint, not necessarily the national team, but my team at Fujitsu, where I coached for 10 years, plays not much different than the national team. Styles are very, very similar. There's not a huge difference," Toews explained. "But I don't want to say that we can just bring what Japan does to the Filipino national team, the Gilas. It's not only that you should not copy someone completely because you lose the essence of the players that you're coaching and what they do well, but at the same time, I feel like there's a lot of areas that we can tune up and we will imitate," he furthered. As it stands, Toews has pieces to work on with Gilas especially with the return of Jack Animam and the rise of Kacey Dela Rosa’s play. He also has Gilas mainstays Janine Pontejos and Afril Bernardino as well as young and promising prospects in Sophia Dignadice and Tiffany Reyes among others.

Hotel bill dispute sparks police standoff in QC. A 55-year-old American guest got into a standoff with police officers after allegedly refusing to settle his hotel charges and causing a disturbance at a hotel in Barangay Ramon Magsaysay, Quezon City, on Wednesday afternoon, Aug. 5. Police identified the suspect only as alias “James,” 55. Hotel management sought help from barangay officials before calling the Project 6 Police Station (PS 15) after discovering that the suspect had allegedly failed to settle his hotel accommodation charges. The suspect checked into the hotel on July 18 and occupied Room 371 on the third floor until Aug. 5. Responding officers repeatedly knocked on the suspect's room, but he allegedly shouted profanities, disturbed other hotel guests, and repeatedly struck the door from inside. Police officers, with the consent of hotel management, forcibly entered the room after the suspect continued refusing to come out. Authorities said the suspect attempted to strike the officers with a wooden object, prompting them to restrain and arrest him at around 3:30 p.m. on Aug. 5. He will face charges for alarms and scandals and resistance and disobedience to a person in authority or their agents before the Quezon City Prosecutor's Office.

MPD nabs man for alleged online exploitation of minor. A 37-year-old man was arrested for allegedly exploiting and threatening a 16-year-old girl he met through Facebook in Sta. Cruz, Manila, the Manila Police District (MPD) said. Police identified the suspect as “Jeffrey,” a resident of Barangay 310, Sta. Cruz. Based on the victim’s account, a Facebook user using the name “Chezter Diaz” added her on the social media platform sometime in July. The two later began communicating online. At around 11 p.m. on Aug. 5, the suspect allegedly offered the victim P2,000 in exchange for showing her private parts during a video call. Police said the suspect later asked the victim to meet him in person and allegedly threatened to send the recorded video to one of her friends if she refused. Fearing that the video would be circulated, the victim agreed to meet the suspect but informed her family about the situation before leaving. The suspect allegedly brought the victim inside his residence along Oroquieta Street in Barangay 310, where he committed acts of lasciviousness against her. Personnel of the MPD Sta. Cruz Police Station conducted a follow-up operation and arrested the suspect at around 3:50 a.m. on Aug. 6. The suspect will face charges for violation of Republic Act No. 11930, or the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials Act.

P6.5-M smuggled cigarettes intercepted in Zamboanga City. ZAMBOANGA CITY – Police seized smuggled cigarettes valued at P6.5 million and arrested two individuals in a law enforcement operation here on Thursday afternoon. Police Lt. Col. Joel Senogat Jr., commander of the 2nd Zamboanga City Mobile Force Company (ZCMFC), identified the suspects as Abdullah and Hussin. Senogat said they were apprehended when the operating team intercepted a motorboat at about 3:30 p.m. while patrolling near Layag-Layag Island, Barangay Talon-Talon. "Upon inspection, the vessel was found loaded with suspected smuggled cigarettes. The crew failed to present valid shipping or transport documents for the cargo," he said in his report Friday. Recovered from the suspects were 2,182 reams of assorted smuggled cigarettes with an estimated market value of P6.5 million. The motorboat and cargo were towed to the 2nd ZCMFC wharf on RT Lim Boulevard, Barangay Baliwasan, this city. The contraband will be turned over to the Bureau of Customs for proper disposition. The 2nd ZCMFC, as a seaborne unit, frequently conducts maritime patrol operations within the territorial waters of Zamboanga City to strengthen coastal security against the entry of contraband and ensure public safety. (With a report from PNA)

Lacson calls for end to impunity in illegal reclamation ops in Taguig. Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson on Friday, August 7 called for an end to the impunity that has accompanied the unabated and illegal reclamation operations disguised as flood control and mitigation projects in the Taguig side of Laguna Lake for several years. Lacson said these illegal activities in the political bailiwick of Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano and his wife, Mayor Lani Cayetano, must end and give way to justice and accountability. Lacson noted that the operations had been allowed to continue even though there were questions over their legality and effectiveness in addressing flooding in Taguig City. All these, while the Cayetanos wielded their power and influence to harass officials of the agencies tasked to protect Laguna Lake, the senator said. “The Cayetanos have disguised these unabated and illegal reclamation operations in the Taguig side of Laguna Lake as flood control and mitigation projects for several years now, using their power and influence to harass officials of the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA), Laguna Lake Development Authority (LLDA) and other agencies tasked to protect the lake,” Lacson said. He also said that based on his team's latest count, the number of “grossly anomalous flood control projects” in the area have reached 32 and is still counting. In a post on X, Friday morning, the former national police chief cited a report on "24 Oras" showing the investigation into questionable projects in the Taguig portion of Laguna Lake began in late 2025 after it was discovered that the city government failed to coordinate with concerned agencies and comply with other procedures. According to Lacson, the former Senate president had harassed officials of the PRA while the probe was ongoing. “Exposed! Impunity has its own limits. Maybe it’s time for justice and accountability to take over,” said Lacson, who earned a reputation for his anti-corruption advocacy. https://x.com/iampinglacson/status/2085514526385209458 Based on the report, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) had flagged flood control projects in Taguig City as early as October 2025. It said tarpaulins at the sites of two projects showed they were being implemented by the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH). One project in Barangay Lower Bicutan listed Topnotch Catalyst Builders Inc. as its contractor and had a cost of P94,047,204.22, funded under the 2025 General Appropriations Act (GAA). At the Lakeshore Complex reclamation site, a tarpaulin showed a multi-purpose building project costing P49,901,230.48. At an adjacent reclamation site, another tarpaulin indicated a project for the "improvement of Laguna Lakeshore area," with Topnotch Catalyst Builders as the contractor, and with a cost of P94,066,688.38. Two other projects in the Taguig portion of Laguna Lake involved the rehabilitation of flood mitigation structures, one at Phase 4 and the other at Phase 5. Both had Dahl Construction Corp. as contractor, and a similar cost of P141,854,714.79 for Phase 4 and P141,854,617.45 for Phase 5. The LLDA claimed the Taguig City government did not coordinate with it on the projects. LLDA general manager Leopoldo Parumog said a public consultation and the needed certificates are needed before any construction can begin in the area. Lacson also recalled that PRA officials who met with him and his staff earlier this week revealed that Cayetano harassed their colleagues during deliberations for the 2026 budget last November. “That’s why Cayetano harassed the PRA officials during the November 2025 budget plenary deliberations of the Office of the President, PRA being under the OP. That’s as revealed to us by the PRA officials when we met with them early this week,” he said.

Teodoro says officials should not be labeled pro-China without proof after VP Sara's dare. Department of National Defense (DND) Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. on Friday, Aug. 7, said the government should not label Filipinos as pro-China based only on their beliefs as debate intensified over officials accused of siding with Beijing in the West Philippine Sea (WPS). Teodoro said the DND uses “objective criteria” when dealing with matters that could affect the reputation of citizens. “The DND works on objective criteria and no other standard in cases involving the reputation of our citizens,” Teodoro said in a statement. Earlier, Vice President Sara Duterte challenged him to identify the government officials he was referring to when he called on those siding with China on the WPS issue to consider resigning. Duterte said officials should be named so Filipinos would know who Teodoro was referring to, adding that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. could be among those being suspected if no names were released. Teodoro previously stated that elected officials who could not stand by the country's position on the WPS should either resign or bring the matter before the Supreme Court, a position backed by Malacañang. The defense chief said the standard for determining whether an official should be considered opposed to the government's position involves both opposition to Administrative Order (AO) No. 29, issued in 2012 to formally define the WPS, and refusal to recognize it. “In this situation, the standard is simple: who not only opposes AO29, but also refuses to recognize it, both elements being necessary, especially in light of our recent filing of nautical charts for Bajo de Masinloc and Panatag,” he said. Teodoro also rejected the use of unverified labels against Filipinos based solely on their political beliefs. “In the same way that red-tagging and other such ad hoc practices are not employed by this organization, tagging Filipinos on the basis of belief rather than covert or overt acts is not done by the Defense Department,” he said. Tarriela joins convo While the DND did not provide a list of alleged pro-China officials, Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) spokesperson for WPS Rear Adm. Jay Tarriela outlined actions that could supposedly amount to betrayal of the country. “I do not have a list of the names of government officials who are pro-China or siding with China, but these are my guidelines for saying that a person is a traitor to our country, the Philippines,” Tarriela said. Among the acts he cited were refusing to stand up for WPS while frightening Filipinos by saying the country could be dragged into war, saying the Philippines would be better off as a province of China and openly expressing love for Chinese President Xi Jinping. He also cited remaining silent when China pressures PCG, Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), and Filipino fishermen, including the absence of condemnation or support. Tarriela also listed opposition to the government's transparency initiative and the public release of incidents in WPS, saying he would also consider it a concern when a person is close to the Chinese government while moving away from countries that support international law. He further cited questioning the Philippines’ position on the WPS, calling for the Kalayaan Island Group to be given up and dismissing the 2016 arbitral ruling as “just a piece of paper.” Tarriela also pointed to spreading false information about the WPS and using the issue during political campaigns without fulfilling promises made to defend the country's maritime rights. Retired generals back DND The controversy has also drawn support from retired military and police officials as the Association of Generals and Flag Officers (AGFO) backed the DND's position and reminded public officials of their constitutional duties. “Public office is a sacred public trust. Every public official is bound by a solemn oath to bear true faith and allegiance to the flag and the Republic, and to strictly obey and execute the laws of the land, including Administrative Order No. 29, series of 2012, which formally defines the WPS,” the group said. AGFO said its position is based on three core imperatives: adherence to legal obligations, solidarity with troops and maritime communities, and responsible and contextual reporting. The group reaffirmed its commitment to a peaceful, secure and sovereign Philippines and called on public servants to remain united in upholding the rule of law.

Annie Ramirez and Kimberly Custodio struck gold medals in the 2026 JJIF World Championships which serves as a fitting warm-up for PH grapplers ahead of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games next month. Ramirez defeated Diana Lomei from Ukraine, 9-2, to rule the women’s -57 kilogram class while Custodio dominated the women’s -45kg class after sweeping her four matches, including one against compatriot Eliecha Zoe Malilay to claim the gold. Malilay still landed on the podium with a bronze. The win for the 35-year-old Ramirez marked her third gold medal in the JJIF world meet after also winning the gi and no-gi categories in the same class in the 2025 edition in Bangkok, Thailand. UP College of Law bans AI and gadgets in JD classes. The University of the Philippines (UP) College of Law will prohibit the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) and digital devices in most first-year Juris Doctor (JD) classes starting Academic Year 2026-2027, in one of the strictest AI policies yet adopted by a Philippine law school. The Regular Faculty of UP College of Law approved the policy, titled "Philippine Legal Education in the Time of Artificial Intelligence I: Recommitting to the Fundamentals of Legal Analysis," on August 4, 2026. It was published on the college's website on August 5. Why UP Law is cracking down on AI According to the policy, the move follows faculty observations of a marked decline in students' reasoning and argumentation skills that coincided with regular AI use for case briefing, in-class recitation, and legal research. The college said employer feedback on recent graduates echoed the same concern, that many students have become not just AI-literate, but AI-dependent. The faculty also pointed to a pattern in the college's disciplinary records: Students repeatedly turning to AI tools for exams and writing requirements even when the practice was explicitly prohibited. While acknowledging that AI has been praised by legal scholars and even the Philippine judiciary for its potential to improve legal research and access to justice, the faculty said unsupervised AI use by lawyers who lack a firm grasp of legal fundamentals risks malpractice and the "dehumanization" of legal practice. Key provisions of the new policy The policy applies to first-year JD core subjects, those traditionally covered in the Philippine Bar Examinations, and introduces the following rules: Onsite, offline instruction. Core subjects must be taught fully onsite, except in exigent circumstances, make-up classes, or when the Dean grants an exception. Phones, laptops, tablets, smartwatches, smart glasses, and recorders are banned during onsite core classes for any purpose, including notetaking, unless an instructor allows a device for a specific class activity or exigent circumstance. Midterm and final exams for core subjects must be taken individually, offline, and onsite. The policy clarifies this does not require "clean desk" exams or bar open-book exams, which remain at each professor's discretion. AI-free legal writing. For academic papers and legal memos, particularly in research and method courses, students are barred from using generative AI at any stage — from conceptualization to drafting, editing, and grammar-checking — and from using research databases that rely principally on AI. In core-subject assessments, simply having a digital or electronic device on one's person, even unused, will be treated as an academic integrity violation subject to formal disciplinary action. Faculty may introduce AI-based research tools only with the endorsement of the college's Legal Research Cluster, after students have mastered research fundamentals, and subject to mandatory student disclosures on the scope of AI use in every draft and final output. The Legal Research Cluster, working with the college's Faculty Colloquium on Technology, Legal Education and Law Practice, will publish a list of approved non-AI-reliant legal databases for use in research and method courses. Part of a broader "AI-Resilient" teaching strategy UP Law framed the policy as a first step toward developing what it called an "AI-resilient" pedagogy, referencing similar measures recently announced by law schools abroad, including the University of Chicago Law School and UC Berkeley School of Law. The college said the policy will initially apply only to first-year students, with the Colloquium tasked to monitor its effects and eventually craft an equivalent policy for upper-year JD courses. Rationale: Preserving skills AI cannot replace The faculty said the goal is not to reject AI outright but to ensure students master skills that generative AI cannot replicate — deriving legal arguments from language and social context, working within the gaps of the law, and applying legal reasoning in a persuasive, ethical, and humane way. The policy also took a philosophical swipe at how generative AI tools operate, noting that such systems tend to present oversimplified, overly authoritative answers and to "pander" to users, in contrast to the critical distrust, patience, and tolerance for uncertainty the college wants to instill in future lawyers. What this means for incoming JD students Incoming and current first-year JD students at UP Diliman's Malcolm Hall should expect a return to fully in-person, lecture-and-recitation-style instruction for bar subjects, with laptops and phones off the table in the classroom and during exams. Students who wish to use AI-assisted research tools in permitted courses will need to disclose their usage in every draft they submit.

Blue Ribbon to leave all flood control cases to Ombudsman — Tulfo. Senate Blue Ribbon Committee chairperson Senator Erwin Tulfo on Friday, Aug. 7, said the panel will leave all flood control-related cases to the Office of the Ombudsman (OMB). Earlier, Tulfo and Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian had a closed-door coordination meeting with Ombudsman Jesus Crispin “Boying” Remulla at the OMB Central Office in Quezon City. “Pero initially, napag-usapan namin ni Ombudsman na everything that has to do with flood control, sila na maghahawak kasi ang dami na ring ongoing (Initially, the Ombudsman and I agreed that they would handle everything related to flood control because there are already many ongoing cases),” Tulfo told reporters covering the OMB. “Tumatakbo na yung mga na-submit ng ICI sa kanila, yung mga congressmen, yung mga cong-tractors, at tsaka contractors, other government officials, mga kasamahan namin sa Senate and ranking officials, gumugulong na (The cases submitted to them by the ICI [Independent Commission for Infrastructure], involving congressmen, contractors, other government officials, some of our colleagues in the Senate, and ranking officials, are already moving forward),” he added. He noted that Remulla had requested to handle all cases related to the flood control controversy. The Blue Ribbon Committee, according to Tulfo, does not want to interfere with the ongoing cases as doing so could derail them. “So, kung baka pakialaman pa namin, mapurnada pa (If we interfere, we might end up derailing it), and we don’t want to do that,” he said. “So what he was saying, ‘Kami nang bahala,’ maybe you can start looking for, ika nga, other mga cases pag may mga dinala sa amin sa Senate (So what he was saying was, ‘We’ll take care of it,’ maybe you can start looking into other cases that are brought to the Senate),” he added. The senator said the Blue Ribbon Committee initially had turned over some documents to the OMB, which he said contributed to the case involving former House Speaker Martin Romualdez moving forward. “Initially, nagbigay na ng, ika nga, docs yung BRC dito sa Ombudsman. Kaya nga, ‘yun nga, gumulong na ‘yung kaso ni former Speaker at yung mga statements mula sa Blue Ribbon hearing (Initially, the Blue Ribbon Committee had already provided documents to the Ombudsman. That is why the case involving the former Speaker moved forward, based on statements from the Blue Ribbon hearing),” said Tulfo. Asked whether all Blue Ribbon Committee documents would be turned over to the Ombudsman, he said the matter would first have to be discussed with the panel’s majority and minority members and would require their approval. “Well, we’ll just have to turn it over. But we’ll have to, ika nga, we’ll have to meet with the entire membership para pag-usapan namin yan. Both the majority and minority members of the Blue Ribbon (Well, we’ll just have to turn it over. But we’ll have to meet with the entire membership, both the majority and minority members of the Blue Ribbon Committee, to discuss it),” he stated. In aid of legislation Tulfo stressed that the Blue Ribbon Committee’s role is primarily legislative and that its hearings are conducted for fact-finding in aid of legislation, not for prosecution. “Ang problema po kasi, ang Blue Ribbon is for legislation. Hindi namin, we’re not there. We’re not investigating to prosecute or, ika nga, it’s just fact-finding for legislation (The problem is that the Blue Ribbon Committee is for legislation. We’re not there to investigate for prosecution; it’s just fact-finding for legislation),” he said. The senator noted that the committee’s flood control hearings have already resulted in the filing of several measures in the Senate. “Yung result po, marami na pong na-file na mga Senate bills because of that flood control hearing ng Blue Ribbon. Marami na po nagawa. Marami po, 6 yata, 6 or 7 Senate bills na ngayon (As a result, many Senate bills have already been filed because of the Blue Ribbon Committee’s flood control hearings. A lot has already been done. I think there are now six or seven Senate bills),” he said. He said the purpose of the Blue Ribbon Committee is to identify deficiencies in existing laws and determine whether new legislation or stronger measures are needed to prevent similar corruption. “Saan nagkulang yung batas? What do we have to do? Do we have to create another law para ma-prevent itong corruption na ito? Or do we have to tighten? (Where did the law fall short? What do we have to do? Do we have to create another law to prevent this corruption? Or do we have to tighten existing laws?),” said Tulfo. “Yan naman po talaga ang purpose ng Blue Ribbon. Para makita po kung saan yung deficiency ng law na iyon. Para, ika nga, hindi na maulit (That is really the purpose of the Blue Ribbon Committee: to determine where the deficiencies in the law are so that this will not happen again),” he went on.

‘Scaling through change starts with strong fundamentals’ – Kickstart Ventures. As the Philippine retail market is forecast to grow to USD 64.99 billion by 2031, businesses are racing to keep pace with artificial intelligence, new retail channels, and evolving consumer expectations. For Kickstart Ventures, the corporate venture capital firm of one of Southeast Asia’s leading conglomerates, markets may change, but the traits of an investable business remain constant. “Technology evolves, trends come and go, but the fundamentals tend to stay the same,” Joan Yao, general partner at Kickstart Ventures, said during the recently held 32nd National Retail Conference and Expo (NRCE) 2026. AI is adding a new dimension to the retail landscape. AI adoption among Filipino sellers is rising, while the majority of online shoppers use AI features at least once a week to enhance their experience. Amid these shifts, companies are identifying ways to leverage new technology while investors are becoming more discerning about businesses that can execute. Yao identified four recurring traits in companies built to last: community-driven growth, channel fluency, operational leverage, and cash flow discipline. Strong companies, Yao noted, build trust and cultivate communities connected by shared values rather than relying on transactional relationships with customers. This helps businesses stay closer to their customers and respond to their needs with greater agility. Yao pointed to Edamama, an e-commerce platform for baby and maternity essentials, whose parent community helped shape its private-label products, showing how community feedback can guide what a business builds next and turn trust into product demand. Yao added that, “The channels may change, but the core message of what the brand stands for has stayed the same—and this really resonates with people.” Responding to customer needs also means being present across the channels they use, making omnichannel capability increasingly important. In 2025, smartphones accounted for most of e-commerce sales in the Philippines, while the majority of Filipino online shoppers visited physical stores to inspect products before completing their purchases online. For Yao, channel fluency signals whether a company can adapt to evolving consumer behavior. She also emphasized that sustaining growth amid increasing complexity requires operational leverage. Companies that can increase output while improving efficiency demonstrate a business model capable of keeping up with rising demand, giving investors greater confidence in the business’s capacity to scale. Cash flow discipline, Yao noted, demonstrates a company’s capacity to maintain liquidity as it grows. Effective management of inventory, receivables, and margins keeps capital available for ongoing operations and reinvestment. While newer technology may change how companies operate, Yao stressed that business discipline remains an imperative for a company to attract investments and scale.

Month-long Kadayawan Festival kicks off in Davao City. DAVAO CITY – Top officials here called on the people to celebrate the 2026 Kadayawan Festival with gratitude, unity, and pride as month-long festivities traditionally opened with the Subang Sinugdanan ug Panagtagbo on Friday morning, Aug. 7. The first traditional sunrise ceremony since 2019 reenacted the shared history and cultural heritage of Davao's indigenous community and the Bangsamoro people through cultural presentation and a symbolic boat parade on the Davao River at the Tionko Soccer Field. Mayor Sebastian Duterte, in a message read by Councilor Myna Dalodo-Ortiz, welcomed people and visitors and said the celebration honors the indigenous and Muslim communities whose settlements, cultures, and traditions laid the foundation for the city's identity. “This year's theme, 'We Are One, KadayawONE,' reflects the heritage of Davao's 11 ethnolinguistic tribes and the unity of Davaoeños,” Duterte said, encouraging residents to continue honoring their culture, celebrating diversity, and promoting peace and progress. Vice Mayor Rodrigo Duterte II, in his message, described Kadayawan as more than a festival, saying it is a celebration of the city's cultural identity and a reminder of the resilience, generosity, and unity of the people of Davao City. He urged people to thank God for the city's blessings while recognizing the contributions of farmers, fisherfolk, Indigenous Peoples, workers, entrepreneurs, artists, athletes, and families to Davao's continued growth. Vice Mayor Duterte assured Davaoeños of his commitment to building a city that is safe, progressive, and compassionate and invited visitors to experience not only Davao's attractions but also the warmth and hospitality of the people. Councilor Myrna Dalodo-Ortiz, chairperson of the City Council Committee on Tourism and Beautification, hoped that this year's festival would bring blessings and unity and lead to the successful staging of festival activities. Ortiz cited the opening of Subang Sinugdanan ug Panagtagbo led by the deputy mayors of Davao City representing the Bangsamoro and Indigenous Peoples communities as a symbol of the Kadayawan's cultural significance. First district Rep. Paolo Duterte described Kadayawan as a celebration of Davao City's culture, unity, and resilience. He encouraged the people to welcome visitors with respect and hospitality, work together, and celebrate the festival responsibly. He recognized the contributions of farmers, fisherfolk, workers, entrepreneurs, artists, Indigenous cultural communities, government employees, barangay officials, uniformed personnel, and volunteer responders in the city's continued progress. "Kadayawan serves as an occasion to give thanks for the city's blessings, honor its rich cultural heritage and indigenous communities, and celebrate the unity that strengthens Davaoeños," said Pwersa ng Pilipinong Pandagat party-list Rep. Harold Duterte. Harold said the festival highlights the importance of protecting the country's fisheries and maritime sectors while encouraging the preservation of culture, environmental stewardship, and collective efforts toward a more peaceful and prosperous Davao and the Philippines. The grand opening of this year's festival will be held at Magsaysay Park on Friday afternoon. It features its biggest program to date, with the city government organizing 26 official activities, up from 16 last year, and targeting 250,000 tourist arrivals.

Makati cops coordinate with funeral homes over abandoned casket. The Makati City Police Station said it has reached out to local funeral homes and distributors to trace the origin of the empty casket abandoned along Sen. Gil Puyat Avenue in Barangay Bel-Air early Friday, Aug. 7. Police said the casket was discovered around 3:50 a.m. by a security officer from a nearby establishment. It was found obstructing part of the sidewalk. Officers from Poblacion Sub-Station 6 responded, secured the area, and alerted the Investigation Unit, Station Explosives and Canine Unit (SECU), and Scene of the Crime Operatives (SOCO). Investigation showed that the approximately six-foot-long casket bore three photographs of unidentified men and a red banner bearing the words, “Chinese Communist Party (CCP) Greedy Salot.” Authorities immediately launched an investigation into what they described as an alarming incident, following the discovery of four other caskets in Sta. Cruz, Manila; Barangay 54 in Caloocan City; and Barangay South Triangle and Barangay Sta. Teresita in Quezon City. “The Makati police are working closely with Barangay Bel-Air and local businesses to facilitate backtracking and the review of available CCTV footage in the vicinity,” it said. “Outreach has also been made to local funeral homes and distributors to ascertain information regarding the origin of the empty casket,” it added. Makati police said further updates will be provided as the investigation progresses and urged anyone with information about the incident to report it to the Makati Police or the nearest police station. “We understand that this is an unusual and unsettling sight for residents and workers in Makati City. We want to assure the public that the Makati Police are conducting an in-depth investigation to identify individuals liable for this cowardly act,” Makati CPS chief Col. Pedro Alagano Jr. said. Earlier, the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) said its initial investigation showed that the caskets were deliberately abandoned by masked individuals aboard white and gray vans between 2 and 4 a.m. on Friday. The discovery in several areas within a few hours prompted police units to secure the sites and examine the items. The incidents also drew attention because of the political messages attached to the caskets.
